entities.summary:
Johannes Martini was a Franco-Flemish composer of the Renaissance, born in 1450 in Liège, which was then part of the Duchy of Burgundy, and died in 1497 in Paris, where he became a key figure in the transition from medieval to Renaissance music. Martini was a prolific composer, creating over 200 works, including masses, motets, and chansons, and was influenced by the works of Guillaume Dufay and Jean Mouton.

His compositions showcased a blend of medieval and Renaissance styles, and he was known for his innovative use of counterpoint. Martini's music was performed at the royal court of France and was admired by musicians such as Pierre de la Rue and Johannes Ockeghem.

Today, Martini's compositions are still performed by musicians around the world, and his influence can be seen in the works of later composers such as Palestrina and Monteverdi.

'In my compositions, I tried to imitate the style of the great masters, but also to innovate and create something new.' - Johannes Martini
